Renato, you have ten minutes. I have read your note, so please start with the reason, not with the background.
The rationale is simple. Half of the interior of Sao Paulo is not covered today, and that is where our largest accounts are.

I sit in about forty of these meetings a quarter, and I can usually tell in the first minute whether a proposal is going to survive. The ones that die are not the weak ideas. They are the ideas that arrive with no reason attached to them. Somebody presents twelve slides of context and then asks for a decision, and by then the room has stopped listening. So start with the reason. One sentence. If I understand why before I understand what, you have already won half the argument. The second thing is the part almost nobody does. Say the trade-off yourself. Every plan costs something, and if you do not name that cost, somebody else in the room will name it for you, and then it sounds like you were hiding it. And the last thing. Do not leave a meeting without a date. A decision with no date is not a decision. It is a conversation that will happen again next month, with the same people, in the same room.

People in commercial teams often think medical says no because we are slow, or because we enjoy saying no. Neither is true. We say no when we cannot see the risk you have already thought about. So here is what I need, and it takes about thirty seconds. Tell me what you want to do, tell me what could go wrong with it, and tell me what you will do if that happens. If you bring me those three things, you will almost always get a yes, even when the plan is imperfect. What I cannot approve is a plan that sounds perfect. Nothing is perfect, and if I cannot find the weak point, I have to assume that you have not looked for it either. One more thing, about dates. Do not ask me for a decision in the week of a submission. Ask me two weeks earlier and I will read your material properly. Ask me on the Friday and you will get the fastest possible no.
